data.title: Brazil's primary surplus tops expectations in October
data.description:
Brazil's central government recorded a primary surplus of 52.3 billion reais ($9.25 billion) in October, Treasury data showed on Friday, above the 47.6 billion reais surplus forecast by economists polled by Reuters.

In the 12 months through October, Latin America's largest economy posted a primary deficit of 35.6 billion reais, equivalent to 0.27% of its gross domestic product (GDP).

  • The strong monthly result was driven by a 5.6% real increase in net revenue, amid record tax collection and a sharp rise in oil royalty and crude sales revenue as oil prices climbed

  • Total expenditure fell 0.2% in real terms from a year earlier, mainly reflecting lower healthcare spending, the Treasury said

  • Government officials said earlier this week they expect to end the year with an effective primary deficit of around 0.5% of GDP

  • The formal 2026 target calls for a primary surplus of 0.25% of GDP for the central government

  • However, Brazil's fiscal framework allows certain expenditures to be excluded from the target calculation and includes a tolerance band of 0.25 percentage point in either direction

data.title: Canada Posts 3Q Current-Account Surplus of C$4.48 Billion — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Canada posted a third-quarter current-account surplus, marking the first time in about four years the country has recorded two consecutive quarterly surpluses, though it was smaller than expected.

Canada's current account, the broadest indicator of its trading and investing relationship with other nations, posted a seasonally adjusted surplus of 4.48 billion Canadian dollars ($3.14 billion) in the third quarter, Statistics Canada said Friday. That fell short of expectations for a C$9.4 billion surplus, according to Bank of Nova Scotia.

The data agency revised the previous quarter's surplus to C$6.10 billion, from an earlier estimate of C$8.84 billion.

Statistics Canada said the third-quarter surplus from merchandise-goods trade was largely unchanged from the previous quarter. Exports rose 0.2% nonannualized in the July-to-September period to C$232 billion, with gains in nine of the 13 sectors tracked. Exports of energy products declined in the third quarter, but from a record high in the previous three-month period as Canada benefits from higher crude-oil prices. Imports rose 0.3% to C$221.6 billion, led by electrical equipment and industrial machinery.

The current-account report also indicated that foreign-direct investment into Canada rose nearly 13% in the third quarter to C$33.61 billion, driven by foreign-led dealmaking. More than half of the foreign-direct investment was focused on the energy and mining sector, Statistics Canada said.

data.title: Robusta coffee heads further away from 3-year low; cocoa, sugar also gain
data.description:
Robusta coffee futures on ICE headed further away from this week's 3-year lows on Friday amid lacklustre farmer selling in top grower Vietnam, while cocoa and sugar also gained, setting fresh one-month peaks.

COFFEE

* Robusta coffee rose 3.7% to $2,936 a metric ton at 1347 GMT, after setting a 3-year low of $2,709 on Wednesday.

* "Farmers are increasingly reluctant to sell," said a dealer based in Vietnam.

* He explained that if prices don't recover, he expects farmers to sell at most 35% of their crop before the Tet holiday in February, as they are banking on this year's dry weather and next year's El Nino peak to tighten supplies.

* Arabica coffee rose 4.2% to $2.7120 per lb, after hitting a five-month low on Wednesday.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar (SBH7) rose 2.9% to 18.87 cents per lb, having hit a fresh one-month high of 19.10 cents earlier.

* France's main sugar groups Tereos and Cristal Union have offered financial support to beet growers hit by drought and heatwaves, seeking to maintain plantings for the 2027 crop as Europe faces a sugar shortfall.

* The real currency in top sugar grower Brazil rallied as markets cheered news that President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva had picked a market-friendly bank executive to be his next finance chief.

* A strong real deters selling of dollar-based commodities like sugar by lowering returns in local currency terms.

* The global sugar deficit in the 2026/27 season will be slightly larger than previously expected, with a weaker outlook for production in India, Green Pool forecast.

* White sugar rose 1% to $527.50 a ton, having hit a fresh one-month high of $534.40 earlier.

COCOA

* London cocoa rose 2.3% to £4,316 per ton, having hit its highest since late October at £4,335.

* The supply outlook continues to worsen in top growers Ivory Coast, Ghana and Ecuador, though there is ample availability of cocoa for now from the bumper 2025/26 crop.

* New York cocoa rose 2% to $5,545 a ton, having hit its highest since early November at $5,575.

data.title: USAR Stock’s Target Reduced By 69% – A Look At What Canaccord Said About Topline Squeeze
data.description:
Key points:
  • The firm attributed the pressure on USA Rare Earth's revenue to industry-wide raw-material bottlenecks linked to Chinese export restrictions on heavy rare earths and samarium, which constrained output at LCM and Stillwater.
  • Eight out of 9 analysts covering the stock rate it ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy’ while one rates the stock ‘Hold’, according to Koyfin.
  • USAR reported its third-quarter earnings earlier this month, posting revenue of $3 million and a gross loss of $19.9 million on cost of revenue of $22.9 million.

USA Rare Earth (USAR) shares were in focus on Friday after Canaccord lowered its price target by 69% while maintaining a 'Buy' rating.

According to The Fly, Canaccord analyst George Gianarikas lowered the firm's price target on USA Rare Earth to $10 from $32. The revised target implies upside potential of 51.75% from the stock’s last close.

USAR shares traded 5.6% higher in premarket trading at the time of writing. However, retail sentiment on Stocktwits toward the stock remained in the ‘Bearish’ territory.

Why Canaccord Cut Its Price Target

Canaccord updated its financial model following USA Rare Earth's third-quarter fiscal 2026 results, which came in below consensus expectations, according to The Fly. Analyst George Gianarikas noted that revenue declined sequentially to $3 million, alongside a "somewhat temporary" surge in operating expenses.

Gianarikas attributed the pressure on revenue to industry-wide raw-material bottlenecks triggered by Chinese export restrictions on heavy rare earths and samarium. These constraints limited output at USA Rare Earth's LCM and Stillwater operations, The Fly note added.

Eight out of 9 analysts covering the stock rate it ‘Buy’ or ‘Strong Buy’ while one rates the stock ‘Hold’, according to Koyfin. Their 12-month price targets range from $10 to $45, with an average of $26.75.

USAR Q3 Highlights 

USA Rare Earth reported third-quarter results on November 9, where the company reported revenue of $3 million. Its Less Common Metals (LCM) business generated $2.8 million, while its neo magnet operations contributed the remaining $0.2 million. The company reported cost of revenue of $22.9 million, resulting in a gross loss of $19.9 million.

USA Rare Earth expects Serra Verde to record sales volume of at least 325 tonnes of total rare earth oxides (TREO) in the fourth quarter of 2026.

The company is targeting a 4,000-tonne annual TREO production run rate at Serra Verde following the completion of its Stage 1 ramp-up in the second quarter (Q2) 2027. Its Stage 2 expansion is expected to add another 2,400 tonnes of annual capacity by the end of 2027, taking the targeted run rate to 6,400 tonnes per annum.

At its Stillwater facility, USA Rare Earth plans to commission Line 1b in Q2 2027, adding 600 tonnes of annual magnet manufacturing capacity and bringing total capacity to 1,200 tonnes.

The company is targeting finished magnet prototype sales to multiple customers from Stillwater by the end of 2026.

USAR shares have declined approximately 44.62% year-to-date.

data.title: EgnsINVEST Ejd. Tyskland to sell its properties to close the discount to net asset value
data.description:
EgnsINVEST Ejd. Tyskland has decided to sell the company's properties gradually, as the share has traded at around half of its net asset value for an extended period.

The Board of Directors of EgnsINVEST Ejd. Tyskland has resolved that the company's properties will be sold in a controlled process. The background is that the share has for a long time traded at a discount of around 50% to net asset value. According to the latest financial report, net asset value is DKK 281.04 per share, which at the current share price gives a price-to-NAV ratio of 0.48. The Board therefore believes that a structured sale of the properties over time will give shareholders a larger share of the underlying values than the current share price does.

EgnsINVEST Ejd. Tyskland has been listed on First North since 2007, but liquidity in the share is low. The company is not alone in trading well below net asset value, however, as the same situation applies to several property companies in both Denmark and the rest of Europe. Several of them have tried to improve the situation through a combination of divestments, debt reduction, share buybacks or dividends.

The properties may be offered individually or as a combined portfolio, and no timeframe has been set for the sale, as the company places greater emphasis on achieving the best possible sales prices than on selling quickly. The proceeds from the sales are expected to be used to repay debt, buy back shares or pay dividends. At the end of the third quarter, the fair value of the company's investment properties was DKK 1,517 million, while equity amounted to DKK 649 million. The entire portfolio is reviewed and valued by an external valuer every year.

As part of the new strategy, EgnsINVEST Ejd. Tyskland expects to enter into an agreement with EgnsINVEST Holding under which the management company waives its right to sales and incentive fees on all future transactions. If the properties were sold today based on their current fair value, total fees of DKK 43 million would be triggered. If the negotiations lead to a final agreement, the accounting provision of DKK 9.7 million will be reversed and recognised as income.

Until the properties are sold, the company will continue to focus on optimising operations and renovating apartments and properties where this is considered to add value. Projects already under way to develop attic space will continue unchanged. In addition, a due diligence process on one of the company's properties is already in progress. It was initiated before the new strategy was decided, and the property contains a large share of commercial space and therefore does not fit the portfolio, which consists primarily of residential properties. The strategy does not in itself change the outlook for 2026, and the company will announce material agreements as they are entered into.

CEO Maibritt Lindstrøm says:

As things stand now, and have done for a long time, the share price is very far from the company’s net asset value. At the moment, you get a discount of around 50% when you buy a share. That is naturally not satisfactory for our shareholders when we are convinced that the values are there. We therefore believe that they will be better able to realise the true value of the company if we sell the properties individually and return the value to shareholders that way.

The announcement came shortly after the company had published its report for the third quarter. Revenue for the first nine months of the year came in at DKK 45.8 million, and profit before tax was DKK 29.1 million, of which EBVAT accounted for DKK 11.2 million. Positive value adjustments of DKK 17.9 million contributed to the result, and the vacancy rate was 2.42% at the end of September. For the full year, EgnsINVEST Ejd. Tyskland maintains its outlook of EBVAT of DKK 15-17 million.

data.title: Spanish airline Plus Ultra to lay off entire workforce, union says
data.description:
By Mireia Merino

Crisis-hit Spanish airline Plus Ultra will make its entire workforce of 659 employees redundant after failing to find a buyer or investor, cabin crew trade union SITCPLA said on Friday.

  • The long-haul carrier had suspended all of its flights this year and told workers of an initial redundancy plan amid financial and operational restructuring aimed at cutting costs

  • The move comes days after the airline cancelled its last remaining scheduled route

  • Plus Ultra did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment

  • The carrier had initially proposed cutting around 40% of its workforce

  • Antonio Escobar, a lawyer advising SITCPLA, said the union requested additional documentation, arguing the material provided by the company was insufficient to assess Plus Ultra's assets and calculate severance payments

  • "It's like someone going on a trip and not showing you the receipts ... I can't speculate, especially when it comes to the severance pay of the workers I represent," he said, adding the layoffs would come weeks before Christmas, when household spending typically rises

  • Another union representative said Plus Ultra's aircraft were likely to attract strong interest due to a shortage of planes in the aviation market

  • The airline was bailed out by the Spanish state in 2021 and has been negotiating with creditors after missing part of its repayment obligations

  • The bailout is under investigation by the High Court as part of a probe into former Prime Minister Jose Luis Rodriguez Zapatero over alleged influence peddling, which he denies

data.title: TCI Seaways to launch direct container service between Chennai port and Thailand’s Ranong port
data.description:
TCI Seaways, a division of Transport Corporation of India Ltd, will commence a direct container service between Chennai port and Thailand’s Ranong port in the first week of December with maiden voyage of the container ship TCI Surya, according to the Chennai Port Authority.

The service has been made possible through the MoU signed between the Authority and the company to establish a direct maritime link between the east coast of India and the Andaman Sea coast of Thailand, the ChPA said in a social media post.

The service will strengthen the maritime connectivity under the The Bay of Bengal Initiative for Multi-Sectoral Technical and Economic Cooperation (BIMSTEC) — a regional organisation of seven South and Southeast Asian nations formed on June 6, 1997 — framework.

It is expected to open new avenues for trade and economic collaboration between India and Thailand, and to provide exporters and importers in the region with an efficient and reliable shipping option, the post said.

data.title: U.S. Corn, Wheat Export Sales Rose Last Week
data.description:
By Anthony Harrup

U.S. corn and wheat export sales came in above expectations last week, while soybean export sales fell by half from the week before, according to the Department of Agriculture's latest report.

Corn export sales for the 2026-2027 marketing year totaled 1.93 million metric tons in the week ended Nov. 19, up 21% from the week before, the USDA said on Friday. Wheat sales for 2026-2027 rose 64% to 564,700 tons.

Soybean sales fell 50% to 755,800 tons for 2026-2027 while 2,200 tons of soybeans were sold to Japan for the 2027-2028 marketing year.

Analyst estimates in a Wall Street Journal survey ranged from 250,000 tons to 550,000 tons for wheat, from 700,000 tons to 1.77 million tons for corn, and from 800,000 tons to 1.6 million tons for soybeans.

Mexico was the main buyer of corn and soybeans last week, while wheat sales were mainly to unknown destinations and Mexico.
